flavor_text.one_line: A desert faith of hidden mercy, hard judgment, and the sacred obligation to guard water and passage.
flavor_text.one_paragraph: The Veiled Wells place Nisaret above the other divine powers, but the Namarqi know survival depends on more than one mercy. Sun, caravan, and buried seed each receive devotion according to season and need. Priests bless cisterns, arbitrate caravan truces, oversee fasting rites, and maintain the sealed shrines built over deep wells. Their theology prizes restraint, tested truth, and generosity offered without naivete.
flavor_text.creation_myth_summary: When the first desert wind stripped the world bare, Nisaret hid water in darkness and taught the patient how to find it by star, silence, and mercy.
flavor_text.moral_code_summary: Guard wells, honor safe passage, punish hoarding in drought, conceal what must be protected, and never confuse spectacle with holiness.
